CHAPTER 2
Architecture Deep Dive
Clean Architecture, DDD, Dependency Injection, and the four layers

The Dependency Rule in One Sentence
Inner layers define contracts (interfaces). Outer layers implement them. The inner layer never imports the outer layer.
Import Express, pg, Supabase, or any npm package
Define use cases, orchestrate domain objects, define service interfaces
Import pg, Supabase, or any infrastructure library
Implement interfaces using real libraries (pg, Supabase, Nodemailer)
Contain business rules or call controllers
Parse HTTP requests, validate with Joi, call Application handlers
Contain business logic or query the database directly

Tradeoff
More boilerplate in the repository (manual mapping), but total freedom in the domain model. Business rules and database schema can evolve independently without ORM migration conflicts or leaking persistence concerns into the domain.

CHAPTER 5
Infrastructure Layer
PostgreSQL, Supabase, Email, PDF, and all external integrations

Key Design Decision: Atomic Aggregate Saves
The entire aggregate (parent + all children) is saved in a single database transaction.
This guarantees that you never have an application record without its related attachments
due to a partial write failure. Either everything commits or everything rolls back.
id (UUID PK), application_number (UNIQUE), status, applicant_id, commodity_id, payment_*

Key Workflows — Code Traces
Step-by-step execution paths through all layers

Nodemailer sends HTML email via SMTP asynchronously in background
Returns 200 { success: true } — email may still be sending, that's fine

Key Insight
Business rule violations throw in the Domain. They are never caught in the Application layer. The Interfaces layer's error_middleware is the one safety net that translates domain exceptions to HTTP responses.

CHAPTER 9
Developer Guide
How to extend this system without breaking the architecture

Architecture Violations — Do Not Do These
❌ Writing business logic in controllers — controllers parse HTTP and format responses only
❌ Importing pg or Supabase SDK directly in an Application handler
❌ Modifying application.status directly (e.g., app.status = 'APPROVED') — always call domain methods
❌ Awaiting emailService.sendApprovalEmail() in the handler — this will slow down API responses
❌ Using ORMs or adding @prisma annotations to domain entities
❌ Querying the database directly from a controller (bypassing the repository)
❌ Catching domain exceptions in handlers — let them bubble to error_middleware
